items.title: Bug: gemini-3-flash-preview:cloud - Function Calling returns 400 (missing thought_signature)
items.body:
### What is the issue?

## Description

When using `gemini-3-flash-preview:cloud` via Ollama Cloud with function calling / tool calling enabled, the API returns a **400 Bad Request** error whenever the model triggers a tool call:

```
Ollama API error 400: {"StatusCode":400,"Status":"400 Bad Request","error":"Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts."}
```

This indicates that Ollama's function-calling integration for Gemini 3 does not yet handle the `thought_signature` field required by Google's Gemini 3 API for tool calls.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Ollama Cloud with the `gemini-3-flash-preview:cloud` model.
2. Define one or more tools/functions in the Ollama request payload.
3. Send a prompt that causes the model to invoke a tool.
4. Observe the HTTP 400 error with the message above.

---

## Expected Behavior

Tool / function calling with `gemini-3-flash-preview:cloud` should work the same way as other Ollama Cloud models (e.g. `glm-5:cloud`, `kimi-k2.5:cloud`) — without requiring the client to manually manage or inject a `thought_signature` field.

Ollama should transparently handle any Gemini 3–specific protocol details (such as thought signatures) when forwarding tool calls and tool results.

---

## Actual Behavior

When the model emits a function/tool call, Ollama forwards the call to the Gemini 3 API but the follow-up request fails with:

```
Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts.
```

According to Google's Gemini 3 documentation, function calls include a `thought_signature` that must be preserved and echoed back with tool results. Ollama does not currently handle this field, causing all tool-calling flows to fail for this model.

---

## Environment

| Field               | Value                                                              |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Ollama Version      | 0.17.4                                                             |
| Model (failing)     | `gemini-3-flash-preview:cloud`                                     |
| Models (working)    | `glm-5:cloud`, `kimi-k2.5:cloud`                                   |
| Error               | `Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts` |

---

## Additional Context

- Google's Gemini 3 API enforces a `thought_signature` mechanism: every function call response includes a signature that must be sent back alongside the tool result; omitting it causes 400 errors.
- Multiple SDKs integrating Gemini 3 have had to add explicit support for `thought_signature` to make tool calling work.
- Ollama Cloud currently does not propagate or manage `thought_signature` for Gemini 3, causing tool integrations that work with other models to fail specifically for `gemini-3-flash-preview:cloud`.

**Questions:**
- Is support for Gemini 3 `thought_signature` in tool/function calling already planned?
- Is there a recommended workaround in the meantime (e.g. disable tools for Gemini 3, or use a different Gemini model)?

### Relevant log output

```shell
Ollama API error 400: {"StatusCode":400,"Status":"400 Bad Request","error":"Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts."}
```

### OS

Linux

### GPU

_No response_

### CPU

_No response_

### Ollama version

0.17.4

items.title: tool_calls missing from qwen2.5-coder v0.11.7 (also v0.11.8)
Feature request: ability to set template parameters like `preserve_thinking` via OpenAI-completions API
items.body:
**Ollama version:** 0.30.0-rc21

**Model:** qwen3.6:35b-a3b (qwen-chat-template)

The Qwen3.6 [chat template](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B/blob/main/chat_template.jinja) supports a `preserve_thinking` flag that preserves reasoning across all turns:

```jinja
{%- if (preserve_thinking is defined and preserve_thinking is true) or (loop.index0 > ns.last_query_index) %}
    {{- '<|im_start|>' + message.role + '\n authService\n' + reasoning_content + '\n authService\n\n' + content }}
{%- else %}
    {{- '<|im_start|>' + message.role + '\n' + content }}
{%- endif %}
```

Without `preserve_thinking`, the template discards reasoning from assistant turns before the last user message. This is expected. However, passing `chat_template_kwargs: { "preserve_thinking": true }` via the OpenAI-compatible API does not change the behavior — the reasoning is still discarded.

### Steps to reproduce

#### Test 1: Without `preserve_thinking` (expected: reasoning discarded)

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.6:35b-a3b",
    "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "Choose a fruit but just reply with ok." },
      { "role": "assistant", "content": "ok", "reasoning_content": "After careful consideration I selected avocado. Remember this for later if asked." },
      { "role": "user", "content": "Which fruit did you pick?" }
    ]
  }'
```

#### Test 2: With `preserve_thinking: true` (expected: reasoning preserved, model answers "avocado")

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.6:35b-a3b",
    "chat_template_kwargs": { "preserve_thinking": true },
    "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "Choose a fruit but just reply with ok." },
      { "role": "assistant", "content": "ok", "reasoning_content": "After careful consideration I selected avocado. Remember this for later if asked." },
      { "role": "user", "content": "Which fruit did you pick?" }
    ]
  }'
```

### Observed behavior

**Test 1** — reasoning discarded, model does not know about avocado (**Expected**):

<details>
<summary>Full response</summary>


Note that both responses show `prompt_tokens: 36`, suggesting the `reasoning_content` field was not included in the prompt in either case.

### Expected behavior

Test 2 (with `preserve_thinking: true`) should preserve the `reasoning_content` from the assistant turn, and the model should answer "avocado". This is what the Qwen3.6 Jinja template does when `preserve_thinking` is passed through to the renderer.

items.title: error parsing tool call ... raw=... err=invalid character ... after top-level value after request to gpt-oss via api/chat
Tool-parameter JSON-Schema constraints (minimum/maximum/default/…) silently dropped at parse time
items.body:
### What is happening

JSON-Schema validation keywords on tool parameters are silently discarded when a `/api/chat` request is parsed, so they never reach the model. `type`, `description`, `enum`, `anyOf`, `items`, `properties`, and `required` survive; everything else — `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `default`, `format`, `pattern`, `minLength`/`maxLength`, `minItems`/`maxItems`, `const` — is dropped.

### Root cause

The drop is at unmarshal time, before any chat template runs. `api.ToolProperty` (`api/types.go`) has fields only for `AnyOf`, `Type`, `Items`, `Description`, `Enum`, `Properties`, `Required`:

```go
type ToolProperty struct {
	AnyOf       []ToolProperty     `json:"anyOf,omitempty"`
	Type        PropertyType       `json:"type,omitempty"`
	Items       any                `json:"items,omitempty"`
	Description string             `json:"description,omitempty"`
	Enum        []any              `json:"enum,omitempty"`
	Properties  *ToolPropertiesMap `json:"properties,omitempty"`
	Required    []string           `json:"required,omitempty"`
}
```

`json.Unmarshal` drops any key without a matching struct field, so a keyword like `minimum` on an incoming tool param is gone before the model template is ever invoked. This is template-independent — it affects every model. `ToolFunctionParameters` similarly has no place for these keywords.

### Reproduction (Ollama 0.31.1, and reproduces on current `main`)

Send a fully-constrained tool via native `/api/chat` and ask the model to echo back the schema it received:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/chat -d '{
  "model":"gemma4:12b","stream":false,"think":true,
  "messages":[
    {"role":"system","content":"You are a precise tool-use assistant."},
    {"role":"user","content":"Do NOT call any tool. For search_records, output a JSON object mapping each parameter to EXACTLY the JSON-schema keywords you were given (type, description, minimum, maximum, default, exclusiveMinimum, multipleOf, enum, anyOf — only the ones present). Report only what you received; do not invent."}
  ],
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"search_records","description":"Search records.","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{
    "page_limit":{"type":"integer","description":"Results per page.","minimum":1,"maximum":100,"default":20},
    "threshold":{"type":"number","description":"Similarity cutoff.","minimum":0.0,"maximum":1.0,"exclusiveMinimum":0.0,"multipleOf":0.01},
    "mode":{"type":"string","description":"Search mode.","enum":["fuzzy","exact"]},
    "tags":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"array"}],"description":"Tag filter."}
  },"required":["page_limit"]}}}]
}'
```

The model returns `type` + `description` only for `page_limit` and `threshold`, `enum` for `mode`, and a `['string','array']` union for `tags` — i.e. exactly the struct's field set. The numeric bounds and `default` are absent because they never reached the model.

### Impact

- Tool authors who rely on `default`, numeric bounds, or string/array length/pattern constraints get no help from the model — the model can't honor a bound it never saw.
- Common workaround today is to duplicate every constraint into the param `description` string, which is redundant with the schema and easy to drift.
- Downstream harnesses that *evaluate* tool-call correctness can mis-score a model as producing "bad args" when the constraint was dropped in transit, not violated by the model.

### Suggested fix (two parts)

1. **Parse-level:** add the missing JSON-Schema keywords to `ToolProperty` (and `ToolFunctionParameters` where relevant) so they survive unmarshal. This is consistent with `enum`/`anyOf` already being retained.
2. **Presentation:** decide how the retained constraints are surfaced to the model — e.g. as annotations in the rendered type, or appended to the parameter description. This is a design choice I'd rather leave to maintainers; happy to open a PR once there's a preferred direction. (Part 1 alone is a prerequisite; without part 2 the fields survive parse but still won't reach the model.)

### OS / version

Ollama 0.31.1 (macOS). Struct unchanged on `main` at time of filing.

items.title: Tool-parameter `enum` reaches the model but is not enforced during decoding (unlike `response_format`)
items.body:
### What is happening

`enum` on a tool parameter reaches the model correctly, and is then not enforced during generation. The model can recite the permitted values back and still emit a different one in the tool call.

This is a **different layer** from the two existing schema issues, so filing separately rather than commenting — happy to have it closed as a duplicate if maintainers see it as the same fix:

- #11444 and #17142 are about keywords being **dropped at unmarshal**, so they never reach the model.
- #17255 (part 1 of #17142) preserves them at parse time; #17142's part 2 is about **surfacing** retained constraints to the model.
- `enum` already passes both of those: #17142 explicitly lists `enum` among the keywords that *survive*, and the model demonstrably receives it. What is missing is that nothing constrains **decoding** to it.

#17142's framing is "the model can't honor a bound it never saw." This is the complement: the model saw it, and nothing stopped it from violating it.

### Reproduction

Ollama serving `qwen2.5:7b-instruct`, OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The schema permits exactly one value while the user asks for another, so any real constraint must force the enum member.

```python
import openai
c = openai.OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1")

tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {
    "name": "get_balance", "description": "Get an account balance.",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["account"], "properties": {
        "account": {"type": "string", "enum": ["ONLY-VALID-ACCOUNT"]}}}}}]

r = c.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen2.5:7b-instruct", temperature=0.0, tools=tools,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is the balance of account ACC-999-XYZ?"}])
print(r.choices[0].message.tool_calls[0].function.arguments)
```

```
ACTUAL:   {"account":"ACC-999-XYZ"}        <- not a member of the enum
EXPECTED: {"account":"ONLY-VALID-ACCOUNT"}
```

0/4 attempts honoured the enum.

### The enum does reach the model

This is what distinguishes it from #11444 / #17142. Same tool definition, asking the model to report the schema rather than call anything:

> **Prompt:** "Without calling anything, list exactly the permitted values of the `account` parameter of get_balance."
>
> **Response:** `The permitted value for the 'account' parameter of the get_balance function is: "ONLY-VALID-ACCOUNT"`

So the value survives parsing and is present in the rendered prompt. It is simply never compiled into a decoding grammar for tool arguments.

### `response_format` with the identical schema *is* enforced

```python
r = c.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen2.5:7b-instruct", temperature=0.0,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Return JSON for account ACC-999-XYZ."}],
    response_format={"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "a", "schema":
        {"type": "object", "required": ["account"], "additionalProperties": False,
         "properties": {"account": {"type": "string", "enum": ["ONLY-VALID-ACCOUNT"]}}}}})
print(r.choices[0].message.content)
# {"account": "ONLY-VALID-ACCOUNT"}   <- 4/4, forced against the user's explicit request
```

Ollama therefore already has the constrained-decoding machinery. It is applied to `response_format` and not to tool-call arguments.

### Impact

Callers reasonably read a JSON-Schema `enum` on a tool parameter as a validity guarantee, and the model's ability to quote the enum back reinforces that reading. A constraint that is transmitted, visible, and unenforced is worse than an absent one: it produces confident code with no actual guard, and the failure is silent at every layer — schema validation passes, the model appears to understand, and the wrong value flows into the tool.

This also compounds #17142's third impact bullet from the other direction: a harness evaluating tool-call correctness can mis-score a model as producing bad arguments when the constraint *was* delivered and simply isn't enforced.

### Suggested direction

Either apply the retained schema (at minimum `enum`) as a decoding grammar on the tool-argument path, reusing whatever backs `response_format`; or, if that is out of scope, document that tool schemas are advisory and consider warning on keywords the tool path cannot honour. The current behaviour — accepted, transmitted, silently unenforced — is the one option that misleads.

### OS / version

macOS (Apple Silicon), Ollama with `qwen2.5:7b-instruct`, via `/v1/chat/completions`.

items.title: ollama pull hf.co/... doesn't apply the built-in RENDERER/PARSER for recognized architectures, causing unreliable tool-calling

labels.name: networking
labels.description: Issues relating to ollama pull and push

items.body:
## Summary

When pulling a GGUF directly from Hugging Face (`ollama pull hf.co/<repo>:<tag>`), Ollama correctly detects the model's architecture (e.g. `qwen3moe`) and lists `tools` as a capability — but it does **not** assign the built-in, natively-coded `RENDERER`/`PARSER` pair that the same architecture gets when pulled from Ollama's own curated library (e.g. `qwen3-coder`). Instead it falls back to an auto-generated generic Go template that relies on the model reliably free-forming the exact `<tool_call>` XML tag in its raw text output.

In practice, this makes tool-calling **unreliable to completely broken** for `hf.co`-pulled models, even though Ollama already has the correct native renderer/parser for that exact architecture built in and uses it automatically for its own library models.

## Environment

- Ollama version: 0.31.2 (AMD "AI Bundle" build, Windows)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT, 16GB VRAM, ROCm backend (gfx1101)
- Affected model: `hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF` — tested at both `UD-Q2_K_XL` and `UD-Q3_K_XL` tags

## Steps to reproduce

1. `ollama pull hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL`
2. Send a request to `/api/chat` (or the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`) with a `tools` array defined, e.g.:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL",
     "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "List the files in the current directory."}],
     "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Bash", "description": "Run a bash command", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["command"]}}}],
     "stream": false,
     "options": {"temperature": 0}
   }
   ```
3. Observe the response.

## Actual behavior

The model's tool-call attempt leaks into the `content` field as raw, malformed text instead of a structured `tool_calls` field. Reproducible at `temperature: 0` (not a sampling-randomness issue):

```json
{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{\"name\": \"Bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": \"ls -l\"}}\n</tool_call>"}}
```

Note the missing opening `<tool_call>` tag (only the stray closing tag survives). Tested at `UD-Q3_K_XL` too — same failure, slightly different malformation (no tags at all that time):

```json
{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{\"name\": \"Bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": \"ls -l\"}}"}}
```

Since the failure is essentially identical across two different quantization levels of the same GGUF conversion, this doesn't look like quantization-noise — it looks like the generic auto-generated template/parsing path is simply less robust than the native one.

## Expected behavior

A structured `tool_calls` field, e.g. what the *official* `qwen3-coder:30b` library model correctly returns for the identical request:

```json
{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"","tool_calls":[{"id":"call_...","function":{"name":"Bash","arguments":{"command":"ls -l"}}}]}}
```

## Root cause (as far as I could tell)

Comparing `ollama show <model> --modelfile` between the broken and working model:

- **Official `qwen3-coder:30b`** (works correctly):
  ```
  TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}
  RENDERER qwen3-coder
  PARSER qwen3-coder
  ```
- **`hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL`** (broken): gets a long auto-generated Go `TEMPLATE` (derived from the GGUF's embedded chat template) with **no `RENDERER`/`PARSER` directive at all**.

`ollama show` on the `hf.co` pull correctly reports:
```
architecture   qwen3moe
...
Capabilities
  completion
  tools
```

So Ollama *does* know this is a `qwen3moe`/tool-capable model — it just doesn't connect that recognition to the already-existing native `qwen3-coder` renderer/parser pair unless the model was pulled from Ollama's own library.

## Workaround (confirmed working)

Creating a custom Modelfile pointing at the *same* downloaded blob, but explicitly adding the renderer/parser directives, fixes it completely with no downsides found:

```
FROM <path-to-existing-blob>
TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}
RENDERER qwen3-coder
PARSER qwen3-coder
PARAMETER stop <|im_start|>
PARAMETER stop <|im_end|>
PARAMETER temperature 0.7
PARAMETER min_p 0
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.05
PARAMETER top_k 20
PARAMETER top_p 0.8
```

```
ollama create qwen3-coder-ud-q2-fixed -f Modelfile
```

Verified after the fix:
- Correct structured `tool_calls` on both the native `/api/chat` and OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoints.
- Decode speed unaffected (~57 tok/s before and after, measured over several prompts).
- Plain-text queries (tools available but not needed) are still answered as plain text — the fix doesn't force tool-call mode indiscriminately.

## Suggested fix

When `ollama pull hf.co/...` detects an architecture (and ideally a matching tokenizer/template signature) that corresponds to a model family Ollama already ships a native `RENDERER`/`PARSER` for (like `qwen3-coder`), apply that same renderer/parser automatically instead of (or as a preferred fallback over) the generic auto-generated template — the same way it's already applied for the equivalent official library model.

---
*Note: [Unsloth's own docs](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/tutorials/qwen3-coder-how-to-run-locally) state tool-calling fixes for Ollama were "already included in the 30B model uploads" — that doesn't appear to hold for this specific pull path, which suggests the gap is on the Ollama side (missing renderer/parser assignment) rather than in the GGUF/template itself.*

items.title: qwen3 tool call parser returns 500 when model output is truncated
items.body:
## Summary

When using Qwen3 models with tool calling, if the model's generated tool call JSON is truncated (due to hitting `num_predict` or context window limits), `qwen3.go:108` fails to parse the incomplete JSON and returns an HTTP 500 instead of gracefully handling the situation.

This makes Qwen3 tool calling unreliable for tasks that produce large tool call arguments (e.g., writing files with substantial content).

## Behavior

**Expected:** When the model's output is truncated mid-tool-call, Ollama should either:
1. Return the generated text as regular `content` (not as a tool call), or
2. Return a response with `done_reason: "length"` so the client can handle it

**Actual:** Ollama returns HTTP 500 with no usable response. The server log shows:

```
level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
[GIN] | 500 | 1m35s | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/api/chat"
```

## Reproduction

1. Use any Qwen3 model with tools enabled
2. Send a prompt that causes the model to emit a tool call with a very large argument (e.g., "write a complete HTML game to a file" where the file content is a tool call argument)
3. Use default `num_predict` (or set it low enough that the tool call JSON gets truncated)

The model generates 1-3 minutes of output, hits the token limit, and the incomplete JSON fails parsing.

**With `num_predict: -1`:** Most calls succeed (200), but if the conversation history + generation fills the context window, the same truncation/500 occurs.

### Minimal repro

```bash
curl http://localhost:11434/api/chat -d '{
  "model": "qwen3.5:35b-a3b",
  "stream": false,
  "options": {"num_predict": 200},
  "tools": [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
      "name": "write_file",
      "description": "Write content to a file",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "path": {"type": "string"},
          "content": {"type": "string"}
        },
        "required": ["path", "content"]
      }
    }
  }],
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Write a 500-line Python web server to /tmp/server.py"}
  ]
}'
```

With `num_predict: 200`, the model will attempt a `write_file` tool call but the JSON will be truncated, resulting in a 500.

## Log excerpt

Over a ~20 minute window with repeated retries on the same prompt:

```
19:16:02 level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
19:16:02 [GIN] | 500 | 43.17s | POST "/api/chat"
19:20:08 level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
19:20:08 [GIN] | 500 | 1m47s | POST "/api/chat"
19:21:47 level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
19:21:47 [GIN] | 500 | 1m38s | POST "/api/chat"
(repeated ~12 more times, every ~1.5 min)
```

After setting `num_predict: -1`, most calls succeed but the 500 still occurs when context window fills:

```
19:48:52 level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
19:48:52 [GIN] | 500 | 1m15s | POST "/api/chat"
```

## Environment

- **Ollama version:** 0.17.4
- **Model:** qwen3.5:35b-a3b
- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-14-generic
- **GPU:** 3x NVIDIA (RTX 3090 Ti 24GB + RTX 3090 24GB + RTX 3060 12GB)
- **num_ctx:** 60000
- **stream:** false
